title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: PLAC permission preserves propagation laws; parents sin in act
pass_a_gloss: That permission has its own reason beyond angelic or Adamic fall-permission: to stop the spread one would have to tear up natural-propagation laws set by the world-creating decree—prior in nature's order to permitting the fall and to repairing the race through Christ, so later decrees could not and should not rescind it. Permitting the fall does not fight justice; preserving nature's laws, God consults salvation another way that keeps nature. Add that parents sin in the very generation act, so as holy God may desert them and permit conserved nature rather than break its course for their work.
pass_b_english: This permission, besides those reasons for which God permitted the fall of angels or of Adam, has this as its own: that to hinder it it would have been necessary to rescind and overturn the laws of natural propagation constituted by the decree of creating the world—which decree, because in the order of nature it is prior to the decree of permitting the fall, and also to the decree of repairing the human race through Christ, could not and ought not to have been rescinded by later decrees, as I have already once warned. And the decree of not hindering or of permitting the fall is just, because it in no way fights justice, and it was just and fitting not to hinder the laws of nature: and so, those being preserved, God most wise and good willed to consult men's salvation by another reason which would not overturn nature but preserve it. Add that even in the very act of generation and while conception lasts parents sin and offend God, so that as holy he deservedly deserts them and permits the nature he benignly conserves, nor deigns, for grace toward them or the work they are about, to hinder nature's course and break its laws.
source_text: Haec permissio praeter eas rationes ob quas Deus vel Angelorum vel Adami lapsum permisit hanc habet propriam, quod necesse fuisset ad eam impediendam rescindere atque evertere leges naturalis propagationis decreto de creando mundo constitutas, quod decretum quia naturae ordine prius est decreto de permittendo lapsu, necnon decreto de reparando per Christum genere humano, non potuit nec debuit per posteriora decreta rescindi, ut iam semel monueram. Est autem decretum de non impediendo seu permittendo lapsu justum, quia nullo modo justitiae repugnat, & justum fuit ac consentaneum leges non impedire naturae: Itaque iis conservatis alia ratione hominum saluti Deus sapientissimus & optimus consulere voluit, quae naturam non everteret sed servaret. Adde quod & in ipso generationis actu & conceptione durante parentes peccant, & Deum offendunt, ut jure merito eos quatenus sanctus est deserat & naturam, quam benigne conservat, permittat, nec in eorum vel operis cui incumbunt gratiam dignetur naturae cursum impedire & leges refringere.
